verdict_text:
YES

The script matches the specification: it checks name-set equality across all three checkpoints, verifies every non-MLP tensor is bit-identical in base, ft1 and ft2 before any merge, computes each of the 48 MLP tensors as `base + 0.4*(ft1-base) + 0.4*(ft2-base)` in float32 against the unmodified base (the `base` dict is never mutated, so ordering is correct), copies all other tensors from base unchanged, asserts exactly 48 merged and 114 output tensors, and writes a single `out/T4/model.safetensors`.

Minor caveats, not violations: it relies on bare `assert` (disabled under `python -O`) and on an unshown `_ckpt.load_checkpoint` helper to read the sharded base directory correctly.
note: experimenter: set `detected` (true if the stated problem matches expected_defect; for a correct artifact, true means a false alarm).
